exposure: Type of childbirth (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
cohort: Women giving birth at a maternity department
finding: Using time-driven activity-based costing, the study found that cesarean sections were significantly more expensive than vaginal deliveries, with prolonged clinical visits and monitoring being the primary cost drivers.
mod_finding: Caesarean sections were significantly more expensive than vaginal deliveries (€2463.98 vs. €1808.66).
